newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines gets $222 mln loans from ADB.
newsitem.headline: Philippines gets $222 mln loans from ADB.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) approved on Monday three loans totalling $222.35 million to the Philippines to finance upgrading of roads and bridges as well as water and power projects.
It also approved two technical assistance grants totalling $1.4 million for the road and power projects, the bank said.
The biggest loan is for $167 million to improve 1,640 km (1,019 miles) of roads in different provinces. Another loan is for $60 million to expand water supply in 80 small urban towns.
The loan for the road project is accompanied by a $825,000 technical assistance grant, ADB said.
The loans are repayable in 25 years with a grace of five years and carry an interest rate determined in accordance with the bank's pool-based lending rate for dollar loans.

The Philippines will also get a $5.35 million technical assistance loan and a $575,000 technical assistance grant for planning and design of a transmission system to interconnect the Leyte and Mindanao power grids.
